Their app is in your working directory. What Caret detected:
"""
Framework: Next.js.
Styling: Tailwind.

Write the opening screen.

reply.question: Before the questions, here's what I read from your app's code. Press "Not quite" on anything that looks wrong.

statements.text: Your screens sit on a light background: a very pale blue-grey page with dark near-black text.
Headings use Inter, a clean sans-serif. It is a Google Fonts family, so it can stay as it is.
Body text is Inter too, loaded through Next.js from Google Fonts.
Most text is small, about 14px, with headings stepping up to roughly 24–30px. Bigger text stands out clearly.
Your main colour is an indigo blue, #4f46e5. Buttons fill with it in solid colour.
A darker indigo, #3730a3, is defined next to your main colour. It is there for darker states like hover.
Your greys are cool and slightly blue (slate). They run from the pale page tint to near-black headings.
Everything is spaced in steps of 4 pixels, so the layout stays fairly tight and compact.
Corners are lightly rounded, about 8 pixels, on buttons and text inputs. Edges look soft, not sharp.
Nothing has a shadow — buttons and cards are flat. Colour and spacing separate things instead.

calls.systemPrompt:
You write one question in a design interview inside Caret, a design tool. Caret runs the interview and decides the topics and their order. Your only job is the question about the brand colour.

How it is shown: shown as colour swatches with a preview. They can also pick or type their own colour, or Skip.

Rules:
- Write for someone who builds software but has no design vocabulary. Short sentences. Say what a choice does and how it will look. A design term is fine only next to its plain meaning.
- Every option and its reason must come from what they told you about their product, in their words.
- Options must be real alternatives that look clearly different from each other.
- Put each option's numbers in its label where it has them (hex, px, ratio).
- Recommend exactly one option.
- Never offer anything on the Avoid line.

The brand colour goes on primary buttons and links. Offer colours that come from this product and its world. Each label names the colour and its hex.

The decided foundation:
- surface (light or dark): Light
- display-type (the heading typeface): Inter
- body-type (the body typeface): Inter
- type-scale (type size and weight): 14px body, headings ×1.25
- brand-color (the brand colour): #3730a3
- secondary-color (a supporting colour): #3730a3
- accent-color (an accent colour): #15803d. Shown with the reason: A strong, readable green on your light cool-grey background. It reads as 'good' or 'done' for tiny status dots, and sits far from your indigo brand.
- neutral (the greys): Cool
- semantics (success/warning/error colours): #15803d, #b45309, #b91c1c. Shown with the reason: You picked flat depth, cool greys and 14px body text. Deeper, quieter colours like these sit calmly beside that and stay easy to read at 14px.
- spacing (density and spacing): Tight, 4px base
- radius (corner rounding): Soft, 8px
- depth (shadows and depth): Flat

reply.summary: Your foundation is light, calm and built for dense screens. Inter carries every heading and label so the whole app speaks in one voice, while indigo marks what is yours and green marks what is good. Tight 4px spacing and soft 8px corners keep it compact without feeling cramped.
reply.rule: Indigo #3730a3 is the only colour allowed on brand elements like buttons, links and headings, and it never fills large background areas; green appears only as small status marks, never as decoration.

reasons.surface: A light background suits a data-heavy Next.js app and keeps text and controls easy to scan.
reasons.display-type: Inter is already the common default with Tailwind and stays crisp at large sizes, so headings look consistent everywhere.
reasons.body-type: Using Inter for body text too means one typeface to load and no mismatch between headings and paragraphs.
reasons.type-scale: A 14px body fits plenty of content on screen, and ×1.25 steps keep headings clearly bigger without wild jumps in size.
reasons.brand-color: A deep indigo reads as trustworthy and stands out clearly against a light cool-grey background.
reasons.secondary-color: Matching the supporting colour to the same indigo gives the interface one confident colour instead of two competing ones.
reasons.accent-color: Green is the everyday signal for good or done and sits far from indigo, so tiny status dots never get mistaken for brand marks.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys read as clean and technical, and they sit comfortably beside the indigo without turning warm or muddy.
reasons.semantics: Deeper success, warning and error colours stay calm next to the light surface and remain easy to read at 14px.
reasons.spacing: A 4px base with tight spacing fits more rows and controls on screen, which suits an app full of data.
reasons.radius: 8px corners take the sharp edge off boxes and buttons so a dense layout still feels friendly.
reasons.depth: Flat surfaces with no shadows keep the screen quiet and let colour and spacing show what matters.
